reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: The table_size c_int owns allocated table capacity, initialized zero and assigned sc_height only after a successful ecalloc return.
owner_creation.invariant: Capacity records storage size rather than current screen rows.

aliases_escapes.analysis: pos_init reads it by value to choose reuse versus growth; no external pointer to the table_size field escapes, but its meaning depends on the live table owner.
aliases_escapes.invariant: A capacity number alone cannot validate a table address.

callback_targets.analysis: No callback is stored; the allocation selected by the table_size capacity comparison may invoke fatal cleanup before the next value is assigned.
callback_targets.invariant: Capacity decisions can enter owner-sensitive cleanup.

invalidation.analysis: Shrink preserves table_size as capacity, but growth frees its backing allocation before table_size is replaced, leaving stale capacity metadata on failure.
invalidation.invariant: Capacity lifetime must follow allocation lifetime.

mutation_commit.analysis: The ownership state described by table_size remains published while pos_init frees the old array at line 184 without clearing table before the RHS ecalloc call. The assignment at 188 occurs only after ecalloc returns. Failure therefore leaves table pointing at freed memory, with the previous capacity/row metadata still published (M0-MEM-004).
mutation_commit.invariant: Capacity publication is not failure-atomic with the owner.

release_pair.analysis: The table_size integer requires no free; only the array described by it is allocated, and retained capacity after shrink is intentional.
release_pair.invariant: Capacity metadata must not be released as storage.

error_cleanup.analysis: For table_size, replacement allocation failure calls ecalloc -> out_of_memory -> quit -> edit(NULL) -> edit_ifile(NULL) -> close_file. With a current file and is_tty, close_file calls get_scrpos; nonnull table and available rows >=2 allow a read of the freed array (M0-MEM-004).
error_cleanup.invariant: Failed growth cannot prove the old capacity remains owned.

signals_handoff.analysis: table_size relies on ordinary resize ordering; a handler-driven or fatal cleanup may observe it during replacement without an owner guard.
signals_handoff.invariant: That sequencing is not yet a proved handoff contract.
limitations: Source-level growth/fatal-cleanup ordering concern is recorded under existing M0-MEM-001; no new runtime proof or fix is claimed. M0-MEM-003 and IND-POS-F4 remain open.
